# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: The Sea Mystery (Freeman Wills Crofts; Inspector French)

**Cast:** Mr. Morgan (manager, tin-plate works, Burry Port; small, clean-shaven, baggy Norfolk suit); Evan Morgan (14, son, back to school next day); Sgt. Nield (Burry Port police); Tom Manners (coastguard, ex-Shoreditch, ex-Royal Navy, small stout elderly); Supt. Griffiths (Llanelly); Major Lloyd (chief constable, Llandilo, Carmarthen); Dr. Crowth (police surgeon); Dr. Wilbraham (Lloyd's friend); Insp. Joseph French (Scotland Yard C.I.D.; short, stout, keen blue eyes, twinkle; believes in leading people, not driving; enthusiast of methodical notes).

**Ch1 (Burry Inlet, late Sept):** Morgans fishing, two mackerel. Line snags, ~3.5 fathoms (20 ft). Morgan grapples, finds object; takes bearings (railway signal post in line with west gable of large white house; tall mill chimney in line with pier-head beacon). Lifts crate, tows to Burry Port lifeboat slip; crate settles in 5 ft water. Later Morgan opens it with cold chisel: body in underclothes, decomposed. Morgan reports to Sgt. Nield at police station; they go to slip with Manners. Crate hauled to station courtyard. Next morning (9am) inquest-style examination with chief constable, Supt. Griffiths, Dr. Crowth, Dr. Wilbraham. Body: face battered beyond recognition; death from blow on back of head; ~5-6 weeks dead. Lloyd calls in Scotland Yard. French takes 1.55 PM luncheon-car express from Paddington.

**Ch2:** French meets Nield at station; Bush Arms hotel. Examines body: triangular birthmark, back of left arm near shoulder (sketched). Clothes: unmarked, left sock toe darned with wrong-shade wool. Crate: 2ft3in x 2ft4in x 3ft, spruce 1 inch, tongued and grooved, iron corner clamps; eight tacks = label position; seven ~1/8-inch nail holes at each of two opposite corners. Bar: ~14-inch 2-inch shafting, rusted, ~3-4 stone weight. Dr. Crowth: head blow first, then face destroyed post-mortem with heavy implement. French's deduction: murder site had no blood spill. Compares to Insp. Burnley's French cask case. Inquest adjourned 3 weeks. French theory: crate floated; holes admit water. Calcs (Molesworth pocket book): crate+body+bar = 406 lb; volume ~15 cu ft; displacement 985 lb; buoyancy 579 lb; ~1 hour to sink. Asks for photographer.

**Ch3:** Tides with Manners (neaps 21-23 Aug; high 12-3 AM; 5 knots ebb; sea mile 6080 ft). Deduces Loughor road bridge as drop point. Experiment: next day 9:30 AM, crate with shingle weight dropped from Loughor bridge; floats 1 hr 7 min; passes within 50 yards of original spot. Next: crane-lorry theory. Constable David Jenkins, Neath lane 2 miles N, 8 PM Mon 22 Aug; driver reddish hair, high colour, glasses, stout, lorryman; "Swansea to Merthyr" story.

**Ch4:** Supt. Howells (Swansea). Lorry seen: Morriston 5 PM Mon 22 Aug; Gorseinon lane 12:30 AM; patrol 10 AM Tue on Pontardulais road. Llewellyn garage, Fisher St. (Stepney Motor Car Co.): Ford ton truck with crane hired by typewritten letter from "John F. Stewart, St. Pancras Hotel," ribbon black; deposit £300, hire £5; returned 23rd, £295 refunded. Morriston Road GWR Goods Station: porter; clerk Mr. Evans; waybill "Mr. James S. Stephenson… to be called for." Sender: Veda Office Equipment Manufacturing Co., Ashburton, South Devon; invoiced 16 Aug; reached Swansea 20 Aug. Veda item: No. 3 electric duplicator, £62.10.0, ordered from Euston Hotel. French expects to search ~30 miles around Swansea. Gorseinon lorry seen 9:30 PM too, stationary → body likely from Devon.

**Ch5 (Ashburton, Silver Tiger hotel):** Sgt. Daw. Tragedy 15 Aug: Charles Berlyn (junior partner, ~40, fair/reddish hair, blue eyes, high colour) and Stanley Pyke (engineer/travelling rep, <35, sallow, brown eyes/hair) left for Tavistock urban council meeting; mill owner visit; left 10:50 PM. Car found by Daw ~3:35 AM, ~8 miles out on moor, magneto short. Footprints toward Col. Domlio's house (~¾ mile; senior Veda partner). Quagmires nearby. French's four test points: breakdown genuine?; car timetable; night watchman squared?; duplicator disposal? Visits Veda Works (Fogden, sales manager). Letter from "James S. Stephenson," dated 12 Aug, Euston Hotel letterhead, typed, disguised signature.

**Ch6:** Veda routine: docket initials; packer John Puddicoombe; carter; crate lay overnight in packing-shed Monday; night watchman John Gurney (wizened, goatee, bright bird-like eyes; on duty 7 PM–6 AM; boiler-house; sees packing-shed light). Two stokers statements match. Railway: crate left Tue 16 Aug on 11:35 AM goods to Plymouth. Pyke/Berlyn disappearance vs. Swansea crate.

**Ch7 (Dartmoor):** Daw; Makepeace garage (stout, smiling; son); blue Mercury 15-20 four-seater, 2 yrs old. Magneto (Ardlo, Bermondsey) armature burnt out; could be faked by needle but takes time. Radiator full. French drives 63 minutes Tavistock→site (Dartmoor, Two Bridges, Princetown prison). Radiator cools in ~3.5 hrs. Time-table built; all test points tend against theory. Quagmire-escape discussion with Daw.

**Ch8:** Lizzie Johnston (Berlyn maid; darns husband's socks; says Mrs. Berlyn cannot sew). Mrs. Billing (Pyke's landlady, East St.): recognises darned grey sock, vest buttons, cuff-links; identifies underclothes. French threatens her into secrecy. Berlyn history: Mrs. Berlyn = Phyllis Considine; Pyke/Berlyn affair rumours; Domlio flirtation rumour.

**Ch9:** Pyke's birthmark confirmed by cousin Jefferson Pyke (Kepple St., Russell Sq., Argentine farmer). Body = Stanley Pyke. French now suspects Berlyn.

**Ch10:** Mrs. Berlyn interview (70b Park Walk, Chelsea); denies Berlyn's guilt. Ardlo's Mr. Illingworth: magneto breakdown can't be timed without spare; spare magneto ordered by "Henry Armstrong, Westcliff Hotel, Bristol," to Exeter St. David's parcels. Insp. Tanner (Yard). French's idea (on train): spare magneto swap.

**Ch11:** Gurney at his cottage (roses, La France). Confesses he slept through supper (~11 PM). Key/tea doped. Ring at office door ~10 PM. French experiment with Gurney's key.

**Ch12:** Duplicator disposal: parts returned to store; stock cards falsified (loop 6→8, 54 leg castings). French forges four cards. Alf Beer (Lizzie's fiancé, dismissed packer) overheard Mrs. Berlyn and Pyke in shrubbery: "'E knows." French's theory: Berlyn murderer, accomplice needed.

**Ch13:** Domlio (Torview, "Torview" house; entomologist, writing book on moor insects). Burt (butler), Mrs. Burt, Coombe (chauffeur), Mee (gardener). Mrs. Burt saw Domlio come home ~2 AM, wet hat/coat, after car used (petrol 2 gallons; mud). French's new theory: Domlio the moving spirit, Berlyn the accomplice.

**Ch14:** Domlio admits car trip; lost locket (miniature of late wife), fall at Chagford valley; lied to hide. Sergeant & French camp at well; hook-line retrieves coat with tailor's tab "R. Shrubsole & Co., Newton Abbot." Tailor's four candidate names; Stanley Pyke among them.

**Ch15:** Pump (quarry, Mr. Glenn); Daw descends well; waistcoat, trousers, shoes found; duplicator parts laid on coping. Domlio confesses: anonymous "X.Y.Z." blackmail letter, photo of Mrs. Berlyn in his arms (Upper Merton glen; sprained ankle staged). French's seven facts against Domlio; no arrest; Daw keeps watch.

**Ch16:** Dr. & Mrs. Lancaster: Mrs. Berlyn left party ~10 PM ~20 min. Berlyn's bicycle (Swift, no. 35,721, bought from Makepeace) missing; gardener Peter Swann saw it. Pawned Plymouth morning 16 Aug by labourer. Plymouth superintendent; Dartmouth friend Maxwell Cheyne.

**Ch17 (London):** Mrs. Berlyn interview; French bluffs. Ganope (tobacconist, 27 Oakley St.; Chelsea phone). Messenger boy sent to Jefferson Hurley; boy reveals message delivered 11 AM to Pyke, 17 Kepple St. Note found on chimneypiece: "Danger. Meet me to-night at old time and place." Mrs. Welsh (Pyke's landlady); daughter Vera Welsh (typist, Tottenham Ct Rd hardware shop) used Pyke's Corona Four to type US lawnmower tenders; typescript matches Veda, Swansea, magneto letters. Pyke talks: Flintshire voyage (Bibby Line, Birkenhead to Marseilles), San Remo, Grasse, Metropole hotel, Regina, Houston Hotel Paris.

**Ch18 (Hampstead Heath):** French shadows Pyke by tube (Charing Cross → Hampstead). Hears Pyke and Mrs. Berlyn overheard; plan: Pyke to confess to French and let Berlyn escape. Pyke and Mrs. Berlyn escape by roof/yard; Mrs. Berlyn's room door locked, 30ft window. French blunders.

**Ch19:** Hawkins (Flintshire purser) confirms both Pykes aboard. Houston Hotel register 21 July: Stanley in room 346, Jefferson 351; basin broken. Kepple St: Jefferson's rooms occupied since 22 July (Jefferson absent at crime and Swansea crate times). Argentine & Riviera police confirm. Taxi driver William Service: picked up man at Kepple St., took woman to Victory Place (Perrin flat No. 19, top floor, Elephant & Castle). French arrests in flat: "Jefferson" = Stanley Pyke, automatic pistol. Ploy: French fakes Carter's arrival; struggle; pistol shot grazes French's head; Mrs. Berlyn comes in, chokes French; Carter arrives, rescues.

**Ch20 (Conclusion):** Stanley Pyke impersonated Jefferson (padded underclothes, shoes, rubber cheek discs, glasses, dyed hair). Jefferson died Nice (appendicitis) ~late July. Plot: Berlyn sandbagged at roadside by Pyke; Mrs. Berlyn drugged Gurney, changed magneto; Pyke dropped Pyke's suit and clothes in Domlio's well, rode bicycle to Plymouth. Berlyn's body in crate under Pyke's name, Pyke dyed to look like Berlyn. Blackmail letter forged by Pyke. Fraud on Jefferson's Argentine estate. Pyke and Mrs. Berlyn hanged; French's chief-inspectorship and near-death lesson. Evan Morgan's fishing trip started everything.

## BOOK 2: Adele Doring at Boarding-School (Grace May North)

**Cast:** Adele Doring (14, eighth grade; rose tam; nut-brown curls; "Mumsie," "Giant Daddy"; brother Jack); Carol Lorens (15; new Sunnyside girl; brother Peter, twins David & Dorothy; parents, Mr. & Mrs. Lorens; lawyer father); Rosamond "Rosie" Wright (yellow curls); Betty "Bettykins" Burd (youngest; Uncle George, editor; mother; pony); Doris Drexel; Peggy Pierce; Bertha Angel ("Burdie"; practical; brother Bob Angel); Gertrude Willis ("Trudie"; minister's daughter; father, mother, sister Ruth; "Bettykins" study); Mr. Dartmoor (old, shaggy grey brows, blue eyes; granddaughter Evelyn Dartmoor, lonely at Linden Hall); Madame Deriby (matron, silvery hair); Miss Sharpleigh; Miss Merritt; Miss Berry (kindergarten); Miss Donovan (8th grade teacher, left); Mr. Dickerson (principal); Mr. Haley (riding master); Patrick O'Neil (Irish; with Billie); Mr. O'Rourke (farmer); Mrs. Diggitt & Mr. Diggitt (Elmhurst lodge/gardener); Mr. Ellsworth (grandfather, portrait; dead); Arthur Ellsworth (lad ~18); Miss Louise Ellsworth (aunt); Alise Alderly (6, orphan, golden hair; grandfather unknown; mother's statue at Elmhurst); Gladys Merle Jones (cattle-king daughter, Chicago/Buffalo; false claims of "stately, handsome" father; clique: Anita Ryan, Janet Nagel, Jenny Clark); Katrina Mason (spoiled, wealthy); Geraldine Barrington (English, "Lady Stuckup," father Mr. Barrington); Matilda Perkins ("Starr," Dakota prairie; brothers Cedric and Basil; dog Shep; Bishop Wesley's protégée; mother Margaret Inslay of Ivondale, England); Eva Dearman (Arizona; Uncle Dick; Amanda Brown "Mandy," husband "Rusty Pete," baby daughter); Madge Petersen (chaperone) & brother Everett Petersen (sailor); Marie (maid); Sunnyside Club / "Sunny Seven" (Adele, Carol, Rosie, Betty, Bertha, Doris, Peggy, Gertrude).

**Ch1 (A New Sunnysider):** Adele, early Sept, sings; "hark to the carol of the old school bell." Carol Lorens, new from Middle West, Lake Road farmhouse, Dorchester High-bound because no high school in Sunnyside. Adele, Betty, Gertrude, Rosie, Peggy, Doris, Bertha greet her. Carol's family: financial loss; farmhouse father's boyhood home. Twins hide in apple tree.

**Ch2 (The Ogre):** Carol cannot attend Sunnyside school; mother wanted her at boarding-school for music & drawing; Peter gave up college. Carol delivers Dartmoor legal papers with twins; estate of castle-like home; lions at steps. Mr. Dartmoor (kind, not ogre) shows portrait of granddaughter Evelyn with collie. Carol: "I did so want to go to boarding-school myself, but I would far rather have my mother." Mother: "Every cloud has a silver lining."

**Ch3 (Two Surprises):** Evelyn's letter to Granddad (lonely; roommate issue; Madame Deriby). Mr. Dartmoor proposes Carol as roommate; parents agree; Dorothy offers to help mother. Sunny Seven meet Carol; Doris says Evelyn is lovely. "Queer things happen."

**Ch4 (New Faces and New Places):** Carol leaves by train (Buffalo, local to Linden). Father's advice: "What would my mother do?" Evelyn meets Carol; school bus; Linden Hall (colonial mansion, elms, lake view).

**Ch5 (A Letter from Carol):** Carol's letter read by Adele: Madame Deriby tall, silver hair; Evelyn; room decorated yellow. Miss Donovan called to mother; Mr. Dickerson: pupils to Dorchester. Girls plan: Linden Hall. Betty: Uncle George cost worries. Gertrude: not going (father's salary).

**Ch6 (Betty's Uncle George):** Adele's letter to Carol. Uncle George (Betty's uncle; editor) pays Betty's tuition; "Betty Bobbets." Madame Deriby's letter: room for 8 more, uniforms at Linden, bus at station Saturday 4pm.

**Ch7 (Departure):** Sunnyside station; Uncle Danny (deaf stationmaster); Jack Doring; Bob Angel; Dick Jensen gives Jensen candy boxes from Jolly Pirates. Six girls leave for Linden (not Gertrude).

**Ch8 (Apple-Blossom Alley):** Saturday arrival; Evelyn and Carol; Adele's letter read. Rooms in south wing; corridor walls with apple blossoms named "Apple-Blossom Alley" (Rosie's idea). Evelyn moves to same corridor. Gladys Merle described by Evelyn. Dining room: Miss Sharpleigh; Gladys Merle Jones snubs; Bertha, Peggy fear snobbery.

**Ch9 (Gladys Merle's Clique):** Clique members Anita Ryan, Janet Nagel, Jenny Clark. Gladys wants Carol's social standing; Anita writes aunt; Gladys mails letter at gate; Billie and Patrick near-discover them. Billie: "Nothin' but girls."

**Ch10 (Downfall of Gladys Merle):** Letter answer by Miss Sharpleigh (opens Anita's letter): aunt says Carol "paid companion" for Dartmoor's granddaughter; Carol's father "poor lawyer." Gladys boasts her father "handsome and stately." Janet defends Carol, deserts clique. Adele snubs Gladys.

**Ch11 (True Nobility):** Gladys's father Mr. Jones visits, uneducated ranchman. Gladys hides; plans to leave. Carol visits, tells story of great-grandfather who refused royal title; "The Making of Royalty." Gladys reconciled; spends day with father.

**Ch12 (A Wish Fulfilled):** Madame Deriby asks for girl to teach little ones in exchange for tuition (Miss Berry gone to brother). Adele suggests Gertrude; letter to Trudie.

**Ch13 (The New Teacher):** Gertrude arrives Saturday by early train; telephone call from Mr. Willis; train derailed onto siding ~half mile; bus with Patrick rescues her. Evelyn's roses. Gertrude teaches kindergarten (ages 5-7).

**Ch14 (Orphan Alise):** Alise (6) says "I'm not anybody's little girl now"; Gertrude becomes "big sister." Alise's mother (Alise Alderly; married against grandfather's wish). Elmhurst estate near school; Haley and Diggitt; marble statue of young girl with name "Alise…Ellsworth" on pedestal.

**Ch15 (Grandfather of Alise):** Trunk "A. R. Ellsworth" arrives; Gertrude and Adele ride to Elmhurst. Arthur Ellsworth (lad, 18) says grandfather dead; Aunt Louise. Story of Alise; Louise: "I am convinced that we have found my sister's little one."

**Ch16 (Taming Katrina):** Girls' meeting. Doris rhyme: "Rosies, posies, violets so blue… somebody must be it." Carol chosen. Carol gives Katrina role of Norah (copied script); Katrina shares Thanksgiving box.

**Ch17 (An Unexpected Spread):** Carol's introduction speech of girls. Party in Katrina's room; Katrina serves feast; Rosie apologizes; Katrina tamed.

**Ch18 (Thanksgiving Dinner Party):** Invitation from Louise Ellsworth to Thanksgiving dinner. Chrysanthemums from Arthur "for all of us"; card: "At the hour of three / A surprise there will be!" Surprise: Jack and Bob (disguised as "Mr. Mellowisky"-type Russians); Donald Burnley. Arthur went to school with Jack & Bob in Dorchester. Betty thinks Arthur likes Gertrude.

**Ch19 (Just Skipping Along):** Snow; sleigh-ride party at Elmhurst; Alise's birthday. Carol wins play praise (Norah). Midwinter exams; holidays; Jolly Pirates meet train. Madame Vandeheuton's French essay medal (Adele second; Marie Le Clerc wins). Gladys Merle birthday theater party in Buffalo.

**Ch20 (The Old-Fashioned Pupil):** Matilda Perkins arrives (plaid shawl, beaver cap, mittens, short skirt; Bishop Wesley's protégée; Dakota). Roommate: Geraldine Barrington (English). Peggy leads welcome. Gertrude explains Matilda's background.

**Ch21 (The Prairie Home):** Matilda's story: mother educated, brothers Cedric and Basil; blizzard rescue of elderly Bishop (wanted to save him from Sioux reservation trip); "Starr" nickname (double-r). Adele lends her uniform.

**Ch22 (Lady Stuckup):** Geraldine refuses roommate; Madame Deriby offers cupola room (ghost story by Peggy about Nina Best). Geraldine reads Matilda's diary. Geraldine injures ankle in woods (arbutus). Matilda helps; farmer Mr. O'Rourke carries her.

**Ch23 (A Dream That Came True):** Matilda nurses Geraldine; Geraldine admits loneliness; Mr. Barrington (Inslay-Barrington family; Ivondale) recognises Matilda's mother Margaret Inslay as his sister. Matilda's brothers in Dakota. Adele invites Starr to visit.

**Ch24 (The C.E.P.):** Closing Exercises Party (C.E.P.). Surprise party for Gertrude's 16th birthday. Donald Burnley, Jack, Bob, Dick Jensen to attend. Gertrude's coach-ride? Dorchester shopping memory.

**Ch25 (A String of Pearls):** Gertrude wanted pearls; Uncle Pierson's $20 gift; she bought black broadcloth suit and lilac silk dress for mother. Evelyn treasurer for pearls fund. Betty's pink muslin dress altered by Adele.

**Ch26 (Romancing):** Eva Dearman coming from Arizona; Amanda's baby. Jack's letter: island in St. Lawrence River (Uncle Jack & Aunt Dahlia's), August camping party.

**Ch27 (Old Friends Arrive):** Madge Petersen (chaperone) and brother Everett invited. Madge and Eva arrive by train with Everett; Arthur Ellsworth takes Everett home first. Pink cluster roses, sailing talk.

**Ch28 (The Closing Party):** Rose's pink rose; Starr in silver-thread dress with silver star circlet (Geraldine's gift). Hawaiian musicians; Madame Deriby in silver-grey silk. Birthday song for Gertrude; Betty presents string of "friendship pearls."

**Ch29 (A Bud of a Romance):** Orchard lanterns. Arthur proposes to Gertrude, she declines for now ("would rather not accept help").

**Ch30 (Farewell, Linden Hall):** Departure; Starr invites all to prairie; Adele's farewell speech to teachers; song "Farewell, Dear Linden Hall." Betty finishes: "Adele Doring out camping!"
